feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This CV is clear, credible, and well aligned to senior digital communications roles. It shows strong progression, relevant technical depth, and solid organizational impact, though it would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Strong career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles that clearly support the “Strategy Lead” positioning.  
- Good credibility through specific platforms, tools, and scope details (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views).  
- Writing is generally polished, professional, and audience-appropriate, with a strong summary and relevant skills coverage.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: show results such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; the skills sections currently overlap and dilute impact.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “organization-wide” is preferable to “organization’s” in “organization’s Drupal platform” if not owned; “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specific positioning, cleaner phrasing, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for grammar and tighter style.
- Lead with your current value proposition: senior digital strategy/communications leadership for mission-driven or advocacy-focused organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter summary emphasizing cross-channel leadership, platform modernization, and operational systems.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial and operational workflow design, and integrated content strategy across web, email, social, and multimedia. Strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, audience-focused messaging and coordinating stakeholders across complex organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid overloading the intro with channel/tool lists already covered elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value, current capabilities will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, specific language: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” and “Cross-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication.”
- Prioritize the most marketable recent strengths: web platform modernization, editorial governance, analytics/insights, and AI-enabled search or content systems.
- Reduce overlap with softer phrasing like “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination”; consider “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Suggested version: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS administration • Editorial workflow & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Content systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, cross-channel communications, analytics, and advocacy messaging.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Make it sharper, outcome-oriented, and focused on what is new at a strategic/technical level.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact + client scope: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 tighter points; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics and governance/usability/ops into one “improved enterprise communications infrastructure” bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/templates/toolkits launched, users supported, publishing teams enabled, workflow time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains, or issue-resolution volume.
- Use stronger verbs and specificity: “architected,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “implemented,” “defined retrieval strategy,” rather than “support” or “advise.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects footer; keep one concise mention here and let the footer hold detail.
- Drupal microsites/storytelling/toolkits also overlaps with “We Are Counties Microsite”; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It can be sharper by foregrounding the biggest outcomes, tightening channel-management language, and avoiding overlap with earlier NACo roles on newsletters/video.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one outcome-led line: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel impact more specific if possible: add email open/click growth, audience growth, engagement rate, or production volume instead of “tens of thousands” / “thousands.”
- Tighten the remaining bullets to emphasize enterprise improvements: analytics stack expansion, in-house studio launch, and governance/publishing standards that improved reporting, speed, or cross-team coordination.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version focused on executive oversight and measurable growth.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older multimedia bullets; emphasize that this was the first broadcast-quality in-house studio and its organizational impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it to emphasize scope growth, team coordination, and channel ownership before the more strategic leadership in 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to show advancement and operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy distribution across teams.”
- Combine newsletter point with clearer impact: “Owned production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable policy communications channel.”
- Sharpen systems/process language: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows, increasing consistency across communications, advocacy and program content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” closely echo the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/owning the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and strategic strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and operationally credible.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Governance for high-volume, multi-publisher web environments.”
- Keep this section purely strategic; leave platform/tool references to the technical skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is close to experience bullets on storytelling/editorial coordination; avoid repeating that language elsewhere verbatim.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. Make it more selective and capability-led, emphasizing recent strengths in Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to execution themes: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first: lead with Drupal; move WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages later or remove if not central to current target roles.
- Replace vague “technical execution” phrasing with outcome-oriented language where possible, e.g., “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Search and discovery systems.”
- Keep this section to 5–6 items max; let the Technical + IT section carry the fuller tool list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep only if phrased distinctly here.
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JS, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and business impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure & insight generation” rather than “Analytics, Insights & Optimization.”
- Use grouped wording: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” to reduce listiness.
- Replace generic terms with stronger outcomes language: “KPI framework development,” “executive dashboarding,” “leadership reporting,” “SEO and conversion/performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every platform here if the Technical + IT section already carries the full tool inventory.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent leadership value, not task-level tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented, broader capabilities: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event technical execution”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the NACo studio build and leadership scope.
- Change “Livestreaming” to “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” for stronger phrasing and clearer event relevance.
- Keep tool-specific language minimal; “PTZ camera systems” is fine, but avoid adding more software/hardware here since Technical + IT already covers tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; consider varying wording or removing one mention.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid and virtual event production” may repeat evidence already shown in NACo experience bullets.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating names only.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (migration, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding version/scope only where strongest: **Drupal 10** if that aligns with recent project work.
- Keep this item platform-focused; leave broader terms like **CMS modernization** and **AI-enabled search experiences** in Topline Skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills entry almost exactly; either differentiate with brief specialization notes or remove one of the two lists.
- GitHub Pages may read as lightweight compared with your enterprise/public-sector work; keep only if it supports portfolio or delivery credibility.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more implementation-focused and trim older/basic terms unless they support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied delivery, e.g. “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation.”
- Rewrite as: “Front-end development (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Serverless scripting with Cloudflare Workers • Deployment and automation with GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) for cleaner, more senior phrasing.
- If accurate, add one concrete qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere, such as “for Drupal-based public-facing sites” or “supporting analytics, campaign, and search experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place.
- GTM may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless you specifically use it for implementation-heavy tagging architecture.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation strength. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and group by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, higher-signal categories: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier (workflow automation); Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp (project/work management); Slack, Microsoft Teams (team collaboration).”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier should lead because they align with recent systems/governance work.
- If accurate, add scope in brief: “used to build editorial workflows, approvals, intake systems, and cross-team coordination.”
- Consider shortening the title to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clearer positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating Airtable prominently in both places unless this section is the only detailed tool list.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar; listing all four may feel padded unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent roles. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise email operations and audience engagement without repeating newsletter details already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add light context in-line: Enterprise email automation • newsletter operations • audience segmentation
- Best version if space allows: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email automation • audience segmentation • campaign operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in NACo experience.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies and work history.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, since leadership and channel ownership are already covered in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve production workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If true, name tools/platforms or scale: CMS used, number of events streamed, newsletters supported, or stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer action, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on innovation/research support and the podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in later NACo roles.
